audience: A lender reviewing a funding request
legal_structure: Not incorporated. The founder has not filed a company.
executive_summary: Northwind Studio sells a shared job board so independent design studios can track briefs, files, and approvals in one place. The target customer is studios with 2 to 10 people. The company is pre-revenue, is not raising, and holds 8000 in founder capital.
business_concept: A shared job board for briefs, files, and approvals so small studios can stop tracking client work in email and spreadsheets.
mission: Give small studios one place to run client work.

values.text: Only ship features a studio asked for.

objectives.text: Assumption: sign the first ten studios from the founder's existing network.
Assumption: reach thirty paying studios at the same price.

team.name: Amina Rahman
team.background: Named in the context as the founder. Builds, sells, and supports the product.

products_and_services: A monthly subscription for the studio, billed per workspace. One job board covers briefs, files, and approvals.

offers.name: Studio workspace
offers.price: Assumption: 40 per workspace per month, set against public plans of Asana and Monday.com.
offers.difference: Limited to the studio workflow of briefs, files, and client approvals.

target_customer: Independent design studios with 2 to 10 people.
customer_problem: Small studios track briefs, files, and approvals in email and spreadsheets.
competitive_advantage: General work-management tools such as Asana, Monday.com, and Notion serve many kinds of teams. Northwind Studio is limited to the design-studio workflow.

market_facts.label: Target studios
market_facts.note: Size this from Census specialized design services counts, then keep the 2 to 10 employee share.

market_analysis: The addressable set is independent U.S. design studios with 2 to 10 people, not every design establishment. Apply that employee band to the Census count for specialized design services.

competitors.name: Asana
competitors.offer: Work management for many kinds of teams
competitors.strengths: Broad product and a large installed base
competitors.weaknesses: Not limited to a studio brief and approval workflow
competitors.difference: Northwind Studio ships one studio workflow instead of a general toolkit.

competitors.name: Monday.com
competitors.strengths: Teams can build their own boards
competitors.weaknesses: A studio must configure the workflow itself
competitors.difference: Northwind Studio ships the brief, file, and approval path already set.

competitors.name: Notion
competitors.strengths: Flexible pages for a small team
competitors.difference: Northwind Studio is the approval path, not a blank workspace.

strengths: The founder already works with the studios the first year depends on.
weaknesses: One founder builds, sells, and supports the product.
opportunities: Small studios still track client work in email and spreadsheets.
threats: General work-management tools can add studio templates.

marketing_channels.activities: Direct conversations with studios the founder already works with.

operations_items.plan: The founder builds the software. There is no outside manufacturer.
Customers use a hosted workspace. There is no shipping.
The founder runs the application and keeps backups.
The founder supports studios directly until the first ten customers.

snapshot.value: Assumption: not measured. The company is pre-revenue.
Assumption: not measured. There are no paying customers yet.
Assumption: founder time only, with 0 paid spend.
Assumption: not measured until a studio has renewed.

assumptions.text: Price is 40 per workspace per month. Annual revenue is customers times 40 times 12: 10 studios give 4800, 20 give 9600, and 30 give 14400. Hosting is 1200 for the first year. Paid outreach is 0.

review_cadence: Quarterly while the studio is finding its first customers, and earlier if a competitor launches a studio workflow.
